title: Signal Tapestry — Prioritizing model integration for regulated verticals
creator: Maya Chen
summary: Synthesize competitive and market signals across verticals (healthcare, finance, legal, gov) to prioritize which model variants, deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private), and console features we should accelerate for H1 2026. Deliver a prioritized backlog and a lightweight scoring rubric (Signal Tapestry) for rapid reassessments.
objectives: Create a reproducible scoring rubric (Signal Tapestry) that combines technical fit, regulatory constraints, procurement likelihood, and unit economics for each vertical.
Deliver top-3 model+deployment recommendations per vertical with suggested console/product changes and rollout guardrails.
Instrument ongoing signal collection (pricing, availability, fidelity regressions) so recommendations refresh weekly by default.
research_notes: Competitive snapshot: several open-model vendors publish low-cost hosted tiers but lack enterprise private deployment options; incumbent enterprise vendors bundle private + support at higher price points.
Model supply volatility: weekly availability and hotfix cadence observed for two large open-weights forks; procurement teams cite substitution risk as a blocker for SLA commitments.

Latency & cost sensitivity: customer interviews show chat-bot UX verticals (fin/legal) tolerate up to 300ms median extra latency for deterministic outputs, but internal API customers prioritize consistent p50/p95 over best-in-class p50.

Regulatory constraints: healthcare and finance require both data residency controls and KMS integration; private deployment uptake accelerates when we can guarantee audit logs and workspace-level RBAC.

Technical feature gap: tool-calling and structured output validation are a gating factor for legal workflows; models with native structured output or function-calling hooks get a strong positive signal.

Quantization/Perf notes: several promising 4-bit variants reduce cost by ~30% in benchmarks but show non-deterministic behavior on rare safety prompts — further evals required before recommending for Dedicated contracts.
market_signals: Enterprise RFP activity increased for healthcare verticals in NA and EU (3 known deals in last 60 days) prioritizing Private deployment or VPC with KMS.
Price sensitivity: mid-market SaaS buyers are moving toward pay-as-you-go hosted options if per-token variance is <15% month-over-month.
Partner motion: two cloud resellers indicated interest in Dedicated bundling only if autoscaling policies and burst controls are documented and SLA-backed.
Feature demand: customer success logs show repeated asks for per-route cost breakdowns and deterministic structured output metrics in Console.
impact_assessment: Product: Add a vertical filter to the model catalog with 'Vertical Fit Score' and suggested deployment flavors.
Platform: Prioritize KMS integrations and per-tenant audit logging for Private to unlock healthcare and finance deals.
Runtime: Run extended regression evals for candidate quantized variants before recommending them for Dedicated pools; update kernel-selection heuristics to prefer determinism in regulated workloads.
Sales/Go-to-market: Create vertical-specific sales kits highlighting model+deploy combos and expected unit economics.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Automated vs curated: Automated scoring enables scale but misses nuanced procurement cues; proposal: use automated Signal Tapestry for initial triage + expert review for top 10 candidates.
Conservative rollout: For healthcare/finance recommend canary + extended evals for any quantized model before allowing Dedicated capacity commitment.
Engineering effort: Building live signal pipeline (weekly refresh) requires small infra investment (ENG-1842) but pays off by reducing manual recompute for PM/SE teams.
